collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Villagers argue over the best way to open a coconut: hold a contest, or let a child show them.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) opens coconuts with a single blow of a rock. (friend) uses a sharpened stick and twelve careful taps. They have been arguing about the right way for an entire afternoon, and now half the village has joined in. What should settle it?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: A contest is held: ten coconuts each. (subject) smashes three into pieces. (friend) taps so carefully that (friend.he/she) runs out of daylight. A grandmother wins, using her teeth, which nobody approves of.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: A small child walks over, drops a coconut on a pointed rock at exactly the right angle, and it splits perfectly in two. Silence. Then everyone tries it. Nobody can do it except the child.
